chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Gene Ramey looks after Bird's lateness
summary: Bird's timekeeping worsened and Gene Ramey took charge of getting him to jobs, though McShann says that was bad for other players.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, listen, Jay, did you -- for that three years or whatever that was, did that get progressively more difficult for Bird? I mean, harder to handle (inaudible)?

Well, here's what happened. See, it got to the point where you know, the time gets bad, coming in, showing up, supposed to make it a certain time, the time would get bad. Ramey said, "Jay, just let me handle him. I'll see that he get here on time. I'll see that he do this."
Yeah, well, Ramey was always very close to him.

Yeah, see, Ramey had -- go by to check him out to see if -- you know, "Come on, Bird, man," you know what I mean, and Ramey used to tell me, "No, just leave him up to me. I'll get him here. I'll have him here." Or "I'll see
that he makes time," you know what I mean.
Which is all right, but that goes on for so long, but then you know what I mean.
Yeah. And it's bad on the other guys.
That's right. It's bad on the other guys, just as we said a while ago, if there's a couple more in there, it makes it that much worse, because they're going -- they get worse, too.
So that's what you got going, you know what I mean.
